title: Chicken Cutlets German Style - Hähnchen Schnitzel
description: When most people think of schnitzel, they default to veal. But chicken has its own merits. Chicken schnitzel is not only more economical than veal, it’s also richer in flavor and easier to cook. The sauce makes a nice accompaniment, or use could use some vinaigrette or a sliced up cucumber or two and/or fennel bulb with some lemon wedges on the side.
ingredients: 1 ½ cups panko or other unseasoned bread crumbs
1 ¼ pounds boneless chicken cutlets, preferably brined in a salt bath for an hour,
Coarse kosher salt and ground black pepper
Safflower, peanut or vegetable oil, for frying
directions: For the sauce: heat the butter until melted and add ¼ cup wine. Heat 30 seconds and stir in a ½ cup chicken broth and 1 TB of fresh lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper, as desired. Simmer 2 minutes.

Meanwhile, prepare the chicken: Mix flour with cayenne and nutmeg. Place flour mixture in one shallow dish, place eggs mixed with the mustart in a second dish, and place bread crumbs in a third dish. Season chicken cutlets generously with salt and pepper if you didn’t do the brine.
Heat 1/8 inch oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. While oil heats, dip cutlets one by one into flour (shake off any excess), then into eggs (ditto) and finally into the bread crumbs.

When oil sizzles add as many cutlets as comfortably fit in one layer, leaving plenty of room around them. When bottom is golden brown, 2 to 3 minutes, flip and brown the other side. Transfer to a paper-towel-lined baking platter or baking tray and maybe sprinkle with more salt. Repeat with remaining chicken.
Serve chicken sprinkled with scallion or parsley and drizzled with a little of the lemon sauce or use pickles or lemon slices, and the lingonberry jam, if you like.
